title: Which of seven figures fit themselves before a full turn?
description: Seven figures are tested by turning each one about its centre. The video picks out the figures that fit again before the full turn and the ones that do not.
teaching_notes: One idea: a figure has more than one angle of symmetry when some turn smaller than the full turn makes it fit. Watch for the slip of confusing a fold line with a turn.

source: Figure it Out Q2 (section 9.2, first block)
video_script.why: The child sorts seven figures by whether a turn smaller than the full turn makes them fit, the same way a square was turned by quarter turns.
video_script.substitution: Trace each figure, pin its centre and turn the tracing to see if it fits before the full turn.
video_script.anchor: a worksheet with seven figures in a row: a circle cut into 4 equal parts by a cross, a downward triangle with a dot inside, a circle with 3 spokes, a four bladed pinwheel with a red cross, an X of two crossing lines, a five pointed star with a dot at its centre, and a shape like the letter B made of a vertical line with two half circles on its right
video_script.payoff_line: Five of the seven figures have more than one angle of symmetry

final_answer.value: the circle with the cross (4 equal parts), the circle with 3 equal parts, the four-bladed pinwheel, the X, the five-pointed star
final_answer.spoken: the circle with the cross, the circle with three equal parts, the pinwheel, the X and the star

maths_rules: every figure fits after the full turn of 360 degrees, so a figure has more than one angle of symmetry only if a smaller turn also fits
circle with a cross, 4 equal parts: a 90 degree turn fits
circle with 3 spokes, 3 equal parts: a turn of 360 / 3 = 120 degrees fits
four bladed pinwheel: a 90 degree turn fits
X of two crossing lines: a half turn of 180 degrees fits, so it fits before 360 degrees
five pointed star with its centre dot: a turn of 360 / 5 = 72 degrees fits
downward triangle with a dot, as drawn, and the B shape (a vertical line with two half circles on its right): fit only after 360 degrees
slip: a fold line shows a mirror match, not a turn; the B shape has a fold line but no turn smaller than 360 degrees fits
count: 5 of the 7 figures have more than one angle of symmetry
video_script.design: One idea: look for a turn smaller than the full turn that fits. Assumes the child has tested turns of a square. Wrong idea: a fold line gives more turns. The worksheet stays on the board all video.
open_questions: The downward triangle with a dot is read as the book draws it (dot not at the middle, so only the full turn fits). Check against the printed figure: a dot at the centre of an equal sided triangle would give three turns.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, about seven figures on a worksheet.
<bookmark mark='cross'/>The first is a circle cut into four equal parts by a cross.
<bookmark mark='tri'/>Then come a downward triangle with a dot, and a circle with three spokes.
<bookmark mark='wheel'/>Next are a four bladed pinwheel, an X of two crossing lines, and a star.
<bookmark mark='bee'/>The last is a shape like the letter B, with a line and two round bumps.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which of these fit onto themselves after a turn smaller than the full turn?

narration: <bookmark mark='term'/>Turn a figure about its centre. If it looks exactly the same afterwards, that turn is called an angle of symmetry.
<bookmark mark='full'/>The full turn of three hundred and sixty degrees always fits.
<bookmark mark='more'/>A figure has more than one angle only if a smaller turn fits too.

narration: <bookmark mark='cross'/>Step one, take the circle with the cross. We test it the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='quarter'/>A quarter turn puts each part on the next part, so it fits.
<bookmark mark='spokes'/>The circle with three spokes fits after one hundred and twenty degrees.
<bookmark mark='third'/>That is a third of the full turn.
<bookmark mark='wheel'/>The pinwheel has four equal blades, so a quarter turn fits it too.

<bookmark mark='ends'/>The X lands on itself, so it fits before the full turn.
<bookmark mark='star'/>The five pointed star fits after seventy two degrees.
<bookmark mark='fifth'/>That is a fifth of the full turn.
